title: Reproduce and report upstream: Hammerspoon 2 crashes when a text prompt opens from a chooser's selection
description: Hammerspoon 2 crashed on 2026-11-23 at 18:53 during hs_countdown-gt's start.test.js: NSGenericException 'more Update Constraints in Window passes than there are views in the window', thrown from SwiftUI's NSHostingView inside the modal loop of NSAlert runModal (HSUITextPrompt.show), itself running inside HSChooser's key monitor (handleSelection calls hide() and then onSelect synchronously). Everything is saved in the configuration's ai/crash-2026-11-23-chooser-textprompt/ (crash.org, the .ips, stacks.txt, the system log); those files hold the user's name and stay out of every repository. Next: reproduce in a minimal form with the user pressing Return, check hs_interactive-gt's M-x path, make the harness wait for a timer after its start chooser, and draft the issue with the AI disclosure.
notes:
2026-11-23: cause found and fixed. The alert stack window's content view was its NSHostingView, so AppKit sized the window to its SwiftUI content; a stack of alerts taller than the screen resized it on every layout pass inside hs.ui.textPrompt's modal loop, until AppKit threw. Fix: the hosting view held in a plain view with an autoresizing mask (ai/crash-2026-11-23-chooser-textprompt/alert-window-size.patch in the configuration). On the branch test-alert-window-size of ~/git.w/Hammerspoon2 (origin/main 8e595e8a, the Makefile commit, the fix), the tests passed in three runs. Posted by the user, after editing: https://github.com/Hammerspoon/Hammerspoon2/issues/432#issuecomment-7099667531. Open until upstream fixes it.
2026-11-23: fixed upstream by pull request #435 (1e19ae13), which closed #432. With a Debug build of main that includes it, tests/run tests/start.test.js passed 14 of 14 and Hammerspoon 2 did not crash. The crash warnings in start.test.js and tests/readme.org were replaced by a note on the fix.

title: hs_whisper-gt's streaming server cannot find a microphone connected after it started
description:
Reported by the user on 2026-11-21: choosing 'Wireless Microphone' fails with 'Audio device not found'.

What was checked:
1. The server's log has 'Audio input device not found: Wireless Microphone' five times, from 17:40:50 to 17:49:02. The message comes from ContinuousRecorder._device_index() in whisper_stream.py, which looks the name up in sounddevice.query_devices().
2. A new Python process with the same sounddevice lists 'Wireless Microphone' (index 2, 2 input channels, 48 kHz), with exactly the name Hammerspoon 2 gives it (hs.audiodevice: USB, uid AppleUSBAudioEngine:Shenzhen Hollyland Technology Co.,Ltd:Wireless Microphone:Wireless Microphone:2).
3. The server (whisper_stream.py, pid 90808, launchd org.turingmachine.whisper-stream) has been running since 2026-11-17 14:14:50.

Likely cause: PortAudio lists the devices once, when it is initialized, and sounddevice initializes it once per process. A device connected after the server started is not in its list until the server restarts. Not yet confirmed by connecting a device to a running server.

The same cause affects the system default. The Spoon asks for the system default by sending no device name. The server keeps the microphone open for --microphone-idle-timeout (300 s) after a recording, and reopens it only when the name it is given changes. A change of the macOS default input during those 5 minutes, such as AirPods connecting, is therefore not followed. And 'system default' is resolved by PortAudio's own list, which can also be out of date. The status and the log say '(system default)' without naming the device.

To do:
1. Confirm the cause: start a test server, connect a device, and look it up.
2. When a device name is not found, and before each time the microphone is opened, have PortAudio list the devices again (sounddevice's _terminate() and _initialize(), which are private; check the installed sounddevice version, and whether a stream that is open must be closed first).
3. Follow a change of the system default: reopen the microphone when the default device is not the one open.
4. Name the actual device in the log, in status and in recording_started, also when it is the system default.
5. Tests in tests/python with the fake sounddevice, and the readme's Troubleshooting section.
6. Keep the configuration working: use.status() before and after, and restart the server through launchd.

Workaround until then: restart the server with the whisper-server-restart command, after connecting the device.

description:

1. Lay out the repository so that hs.spoons.install() finds each Spoon. Each Spoon must be a directory named <name>.spoon2, at the top level or in a Spoons directory.

5. Rewrite the documentation for users. It should explain what each Spoon does for the user, with screenshots where they help, and list the Spoons in order of how likely a user is to want them.
6. Check that every Spoon installs and loads the way a user would install it, and then publish.

title: hs_network-gt: report network traffic per application
description: The user asked on 2026-11-26 for hs_network-gt (the configuration's Spoons/hs_network-gt, not published) to report network traffic per application. Hammerspoon 2 has no API for it, and macOS offers no public one (nettop and Activity Monitor use the private NetworkStatistics framework), so the Spoon runs nettop through hs.task. Measured on 2026-11-26: `nettop -P -L 1 -x -J bytes_in,bytes_out` works without administrator rights, lists about 52 processes with cumulative bytes in and out since each process started (for example syncthing 482 MB out, Chrome's helper 156 MB in), and takes 5.28 s per sample. Rates need two samples and their difference. Processes are not applications: Chrome's traffic appears under its helper processes, so processes are grouped by application through their pid. kernel_task and mDNSResponder carry system-wide traffic. Following the cost rules in CLAUDE.md, the reading is taken on demand, not polled. One possible use: naming the applications behind the Spoon's existing consumption alerts ("+10.0MB consumed on eduroam").

title: hs_selectWindow-gt: show the window's Space in its row, after the screen, when it is not the current Space
description:
Requested by the user on 2026-11-24. A row's second line is 'Application · Screen', with 'minimized' or 'hidden' after it (subTextFor()). When the window is on a Space that its screen is not showing, add that Space after the screen, for example 'Skim · Built-in Retina Display · Desktop 2'. Nothing is added for a window on a Space being shown. This is a narrower form of the Hammerspoon 1 setting showWorkspaceInSubText (hammer2spoons-ei6.67), which labelled every window.

Measured on 2026-11-24 with the user's 28 standard windows on three screens: the current Spaces are read from screen.spaces with HSSpace.isCurrent, in 6 ms; a window's Spaces from window.spaces, in about 1 ms or less each; a window is on a Space being shown when any of its Spaces is current. 27 were, and one Skim window was on the laptop's Desktop 2 (HSSpace.desktopNumber 2, type 'desktop'), which that Space's windowIDs() confirmed. isVisible was true for that window and its screen was the laptop, so neither can tell. A fullscreen Space has no desktopNumber: decide its label (for example the application's name, or 'fullscreen'). Two windows on a fullscreen Space not being shown had no HSWindow at all (hs.window.allWindows() did not return them, though hs.window.spacesForID() placed them), so they cannot be listed anyway. Not yet seen: a minimized window, and a window shown on all Spaces, which lists several Spaces and counts as current when any is.

Cost: the chooser builds its rows from hs_windowfilter-gt's state, which has no Space. Reading window.spaces for every row costs about 1 ms per window each time a chooser opens, about 30 ms for 30 windows; check whether hs_windowfilter-gt could hold the Space in its state instead. Add a test (a test window moved to another Space with window.moveToSpace(), then back), document the row in the readme, and raise the version.
notes:
2026-11-24, the user: about 1 ms per window is acceptable, so read window.spaces for each row when the chooser opens; hs_windowfilter-gt need not hold the Space. Check in the Hammerspoon 2 source that window.spaces asks the window server, not the application, so that an application that does not answer cannot slow the chooser.
2026-11-24, the user: a window on a fullscreen Space that is not being shown is labelled 'fullscreen' instead of a Space, since such a Space holds that one window. (The fullscreen Space measured earlier listed two window ids, neither of them an HSWindow, so they are not listed in the chooser anyway.)

description: Parity with the Hammerspoon 1 Spoon (~/.hammerspoon/Spoons/hs_select_window.spoon/init.lua), found on 2026-11-24. It had: the _ws bindings (all_windows_ws, app_windows_ws, previous_window_ws, previous_app_window_ws), which list or switch to windows on the current Space only, leaving out applications without windows (a space filter must exclude them, init.lua around line 357); all_windows_move_to_current_workspace (selectWindowAndMove, around line 447), which takes the chosen window out of fullscreen and moves it to the current Space and screen before focusing it; and showWorkspaceInSubText, which adds the window's Space, such as 'Desktop 2', to the row's second line (buildWindowSpaceLabels, around line 303). hs_selectWindow-gt's readme, under Limitations, says this cannot be done because Hammerspoon 2 has no module for Spaces; that is out of date. Hammerspoon 2 now has screen.spaces with HSSpace.isCurrent, HSSpace.windowIDs() (front to back), HSSpace.desktopNumber, window.spaces, window.moveToSpace() and hs.window.moveToSpaceForID(). Name the new functions by the repository's conventions (subject first, action last; Select for those that focus a window), add settings and bindHotkeys() names, correct the Limitations section and the 'Coming from Hammerspoon 1' table, estimate the cost per chooser opening, and test.

title: hs_selectWindow-gt: list running applications that have no windows, and switch to the application
description:
Requested by the user on 2026-11-24. A running application with no windows does not appear in hs_selectWindow-gt's choosers, so it cannot be switched to. Add a row for each such application; choosing it activates the application.

How the Hammerspoon 1 Spoon does it (~/.hammerspoon/Spoons/hs_select_window.spoon/init.lua, obj:appendWindowlessApps(), line 229):
1. It walks hs.application.runningApplications() and keeps the regular applications (kind 1, not background or accessory) whose bundle id is not already among the listed windows' applications, and not the current application.
2. Each becomes a row at the end of the list: text '<name> (no windows)', subText the bundle id, the application's icon as image, no window, and the application.
3. It is added to the all-windows chooser (all_windows, here windowSelect()) only when the list is not narrowed to the current application or the current space (init.lua around line 357: a windowless application has no windows on any space, so a space filter must leave it out), and to the one-window-per-application chooser (first_window_per_app, here applicationSelect()) always (around line 515).
4. Choosing the row activates the application: app:activate(true), falling back to app:setFrontmost(true) when that fails (around line 392). When the list has a single row, that row is acted on without showing the chooser (around line 418).

For Hammerspoon 2: an application's kind is 'standard' for a regular one. Check what activating an application without windows does there (setFrontmost, or HSApplication's own activate), and whether some applications open a window when activated. An application that has turned the Accessibility API off, such as Firefox in kiosk mode (hammer2spoons-ei6.64), also reports no windows and would be listed; decide whether that is right. Estimate the cost: one runningApplications() walk each time a chooser opens. Document the rows in the readme, and test them.

title: Restore the focus to the right window when two windows of one application are in front
description: After a run of tests/run, the harness restores the order of the user's windows but not always the focus. On 2026-11-23, twice (hs_countdown-gt running.test.js and hs_window-gt two-screens.test.js), the user's focus was on Google Chrome #26120 with Chrome #26123 in front of it, and after the run the focus was on #26123. Runs with Skim, Emacs or kitty focused restored it correctly. Probably focusing the application, or raising the windows in order, gives the focus to the application's frontmost window and not to the one recorded. Find the cause in tests-common and fix it, then sync every Spoon's copy.

The tests follow what was learned writing hs_window-gt's tests (epic hammer2spoons-cvl, ai/tests-hs_window-gt.org, Spoons/hs_window-gt.spoon2/tests/readme.org):

1. They run in the user's running Hammerspoon 2, on a fresh copy of the Spoon loaded through require.cache. A chooser asks before the run starts, and another at the end asks whether the run was uninterrupted. The front window of each screen and the focused window are restored afterwards.
2. Test windows come from tests/fixture-windows.jxa run by osascript, as a regular application. hs_windowfilter-gt tracks only standard applications, so an accessory application's windows produce no events. Windows are closed with their close button: ending the process produced no windowDestroyed.
3. A test acts only on its own windows, restores anything of the user's it touches (pointer, clipboard text), and binds keys only with modifiers the user does not bind.
4. Tests that need two screens are in one file that exports {screens: 2, tests}, and are skipped as a whole on one screen.
5. A test that fails because of a defect outside the Spoon carries knownIssue.
6. A full run is long. Only the files a change can affect are run.

Particular to this Spoon: a fresh copy starts its own tracker, with accessibility observers on every standard application, alongside the user's copy. The tests must measure what that costs, and stop() must release every observer and timer it created.

Known already: hs.window.orderedWindows() does not return windows in stacking order (see hammer2spoons-ei6.50), and a window closed by ending its process gets no windowDestroyed.
acceptance_criteria: Every child bead is closed. make test in the Spoon's directory runs every test and reports each result. use.status() shows the same Spoons loaded before and after a run, and the user's windows are unchanged by it.

title: Confirm the fix of Hammerspoon/Hammerspoon2#423 and remove knownIssue
description:
Found on 2026-11-23 by the two-screen test 'a window returning to a screen takes the frame it last had there' (hammer2spoons-cvl.2). HSWindow.moveAndResize() in Hammerspoon 2 sets AXPosition and then AXSize, once each. A window moved to another screen and made larger in one assignment can come out narrower, cut at the right edge of the screen it left: 1920 requested, 911 received on the user's displays. A second assignment gives the full size. Reproduced without the Spoon, through hs.window directly.

The draft is ~/.config/Hammerspoon2/ai/issue_unfiled_frame-cut-at-previous-screen.md. Before filing, as hammer2spoons/CLAUDE.md and Hammerspoon 2's AI_POLICY.md require: the user reviews and edits it, and checks again that no existing issue reports it. No existing issue was found on 2026-11-23 for the searches 'frame', 'frame size screen' and 'moveAndResize'.

Not verified: why the application limits the size to the old screen, why a window that has not been on the target screen before is not affected, whether applications other than a plain NSWindow from osascript behave the same, and how Hammerspoon 1 set a frame.

Separate decision, not part of this bead: whether hs_window-gt works around it by setting the frame again when the size read back differs.

description:
Test that each setting in hs_window-gt's config changes what the readme says it changes. Each test sets the value on the fresh copy, checks the effect, and puts the default back.

1. historySize: the history keeps at most that many positions.
2. attachKeys and attachModifiers: only the listed digits can be attached, and they are bound with the listed modifiers.

4. attachFile: the attachments are saved to and restored from that file.

title: Make hs_window-gt's windowToScreenMove() move fullscreen windows
description:
Requested by the user on 2026-11-21: in hs_window-gt, add a function that moves a fullscreen application window from its screen to the next screen that has no fullscreen window on it.

Starting point in Spoons/hs_window-gt.spoon2/init.js:
1. _windowToScreenMove() already walks the screens in order and skips those listed by fullscreenScreenIds(). The new function can use the same walk.
2. movable() refuses fullscreen windows, because macOS will not move one. The likely approach is to leave fullscreen, wait for the animation to end, move the window to the target screen, and enter fullscreen again there. Whether that works, and how long each wait has to be, must be measured with hs2 before writing it.

Naming: subject first, for example fullscreenWindowToScreenMove(), with the command fullscreen-window-to-screen-move or similar; confirm the name with the user. Add an entry to the Spoon's menu, document it in readme.org, and raise the version in spoon.json.

Acceptance: with two or more screens, the function moves the focused fullscreen window to the next screen without a fullscreen window, where it is fullscreen again. It alerts and does nothing when every other screen has a fullscreen window, when there is only one screen, or when the focused window is not fullscreen. The configuration check with use.status() passes after reloading.
notes:
Implemented 2026-11-21 as fullscreenWindowToScreenMove([target], [win]), menu entry 'Fullscreen next' on F, config.fullscreenLeaveWait (3 s), version 2.4.0. Measured: isFullscreen turns false within 0.1 s of leaving, a move then holds, whole move ~0.25 s; 4/4 round trips between the built-in display and the EV2736W ended fullscreen. Checked next/previous skip the Dell showing Chrome fullscreen; refusals for an occupied target screen and a non-fullscreen window; windowToScreenMove unchanged; use.status() all loaded after reload. The menu screenshot still shows 34 options.
Changed by the user on 2026-11-21: no separate function or menu item. windowToScreenMove() now handles a fullscreen window itself (next, previous, a screen, or the chooser), through the internal fullscreenWindowOnScreenPlace(). Retested after reload: next 5->1 and previous 1->5 both fullscreen, skipping the Dell; a screen showing a fullscreen window is refused; a non-fullscreen window moves as before; the menu has no extra item; use.status() all 21 loaded.

title: Follow the upstream Spoons guide on documenting and sharing a Spoon
description:
Hammerspoon 2 pull request 398 revises docs/spoons-guide.md, which is the guide a user reads to learn how Spoons are found, installed and shared: https://github.com/cmsj/Hammerspoon2/pull/398

Review this repository and its readmes against that guide, and do what it asks of an author.

The guide sets no layout for a README. It states one requirement, in the new "Finding Spoons" section: each repository's README should say which Spoons it holds and how to configure them.

Two separate things make a Spoon findable, and both need doing.

First, the repository. Add the hammerspoon2-spoon topic to it, so it appears in the list at https://github.com/topics/hammerspoon2-spoon, which is where the guide now sends users looking for Spoons. Posting on r/Hammerspoon helps too. Tag releases, so a version can be pinned with ref.

Second, each Spoon's own description in its spoon.json. hs.spoons.available("you/repo") prints name, version and description for every Spoon in a repository, so that one string is all a user sees when deciding whether a Spoon is what they want. Hammerspoon 2 requires name, version and description in spoon.json. Check that each description reads as an answer to "what is this for", not as a title.

The pull request was still open on 2026-11-18, so check the merged wording before acting on it.

title: hs_whisper-gt streaming server: change chunking settings during a recording (update_settings)
description:
Requested by the Emacs side (whisper-gt, ~/.emacs.d bead emacs-0a8.16).

Problem: the chunking settings (silence_threshold, min_chunk_duration, max_chunk_duration, speech_margin) are fixed at start_recording (_apply_settings). whisper-gt's command listener records with a short threshold (0.5 s) so commands respond quickly; when the user says 'Emacs listen' the listener switches to dictation inside the same recording, where a longer threshold (1.0 s, so a sentence is not split at every short pause) would be better. Today it has to keep 0.5 s, or stop and restart the recording (losing what is said in between).

Proposal: a command {"command": "update_settings", <setting>: <value>, ...} accepted while recording. It changes only the named chunking settings (silence_threshold, min_chunk_duration, max_chunk_duration, speech_margin), under self.lock, and they apply from the next 0.5 s block; the chunk in progress keeps its audio. Settings that cannot change mid-recording (drop_silence, output_dir, filename_prefix, audio_input, keep_full_recording) are refused with an error event naming them. Answer with an event (e.g. settings_updated, with the values now in force) so the client knows when the change applies. When not recording: an error, as stop_recording does.

Feasibility (read 2026-11-18): the cut compares against self.silence_threshold on every block (_check_silence_boundary, whisper_stream.py:731; drop_silence path :956), and handle_command (:1038) runs commands from the same queue as start_recording, so the change is a new branch in handle_command plus a setter shared with _apply_settings. Note: unknown commands produce an error event (unknown keys in start_recording are ignored), so the client must know the server supports it (e.g. a capability or version in the status event).

Tests: a test-file recording that changes silence_threshold mid-recording and checks where chunks are cut before and after the change; refusal of a fixed setting; error when not recording.

title: hs_whisper-gt streaming server: setting to not write the full recording (keep_full_recording)
description:
Requested by the Emacs side (whisper-gt, ~/.emacs.d bead emacs-0a8.10; design in ~/.emacs.d/ai/whisper-commands.org 'Not storing long silences').

Problem: with drop_silence (hammer2spoons-ei6.55) the silence is left out of the chunks, of memory and of the speech-only file, but not of the full recording: _speech_block writes every block to full_writer (<name>.wav) before it looks for speech, and no setting turns that off. A long command session (mostly silence between short spoken commands) therefore stores all of it, about 115 MB per hour, including anything said nearby that the VAD did not take for speech.

Request: a per-recording start_recording setting keep_full_recording (bool, default true, so the Spoon and existing clients are unchanged). When false, with drop_silence: do not open or write the full recording; keep the speech-only file and the JSON sidecar (they hold only speech; the sidecar's recording field and recording_start/recording_end can stay, as offsets in the stream, or the recording field becomes null: document which); complete_file then has no file_path for a full recording (document what it sends). Without drop_silence the setting has no effect, or is documented as such (that mode holds the whole recording in memory anyway).

Compatibility: whisper-gt already sends keep_full_recording: false in command mode, relying on the server ignoring unknown start_recording keys (command.get by name), so the name must be exactly keep_full_recording.

Tests: a recording with drop_silence and keep_full_recording false writes no <name>.wav, still writes the speech file and sidecar, and sends chunk_ready with offset as before; the default keeps today's files. Update readme.org ('The protocol', 'Timestamps, and dropping long pauses').

title: Format hs_whisper-gt's dictation as sentences separated by blank lines when the VAD is used
description:
The user's request, 2026-11-17: 'we need to update the transcription, if not using the segmenter, do the same as now, otherwise, remove the timestamps, and merge sentences, and add empty \n between sentences. So the text looks better formatted.'

Background. With the VAD (hammer2spoons-ei6.56), the whisper server ends segments at pauses, which tend to be sentence ends, but a sentence can still be split across segments, and a segment can hold more than one sentence. Ordinary dictation now asks for response_format text, which gives one segment per line; the Spoon trims the lines and joins them with a newline. Chunks are joined with a blank line (CHUNK_SEPARATOR). Timestamped dictation writes '[C start end]' and '[start end] text' lines.

To do, as understood so far:
1. Without the VAD, the text stays exactly as it is now.
2. With the VAD, the text has no timestamps; the segments are merged and re-split into sentences, at . ? ! (and 。？！ for Japanese); and the sentences are separated by an empty line.

To settle with the user before implementing:
- What 'the segmenter' means: the whisper server's VAD, or the timestamped mode.
- Whether this applies to timestamped dictation too, or only to ordinary dictation.
- What happens to a sentence that runs across two chunks, and to the text after the last full stop of a chunk.
- Whether chunks pasted one at a time (streamingChunkInsert) still work as they do: each chunk is pasted when it is ready, so a sentence that continues in the next chunk is pasted in two parts.
- Whether filters and processors receive the reformatted text.
acceptance_criteria: Without the VAD the text is unchanged; with it, the text is formatted as the user decided; the configuration loads; the user has approved closing this bead.
notes:
2026-11-17: The user added: 'we can use the timestamps to decide where to start new paragraphs (\n).' So the segment times, which are accurate with the VAD, decide paragraph breaks: a pause between two segments longer than some threshold starts a new paragraph. To settle: the threshold, and whether a paragraph break is the empty line between sentences or something in addition to it. The chunk boundaries (a pause longer than streamingSilenceThreshold) are pauses too, and could be paragraph breaks on the same rule.
2026-11-17: Decided.
1. One sentence per line, and an empty line between paragraphs.
2. A pause between two segments of at least a setting's length starts a paragraph; the setting defaults to 2 s.
3. 'The segmenter' is the VAD: the new format applies when the whisper server is used with the VAD. Timestamped dictation keeps its [C ...] and [start end] lines.
4. Chunks pasted one at a time stay as they are. Chunks are separated by an empty line, which is a paragraph break; the pause that ends a chunk is longer than 2 s anyway.
2026-11-17: Implemented, not committed. whisperserverParagraphPause (2.0). With the VAD, transcribe() asks for segments and returns paragraphsFormat(segments, pause): sentencesSplit() splits at .?! before a space and a word not in lowercase, and at 。？！ anywhere; textJoin() joins without a space next to CJK text. The reformatting is its own function, as the user asked. Timestamped dictation unchanged. tests/js/test_paragraphs_format.js (make test-js) 8 of 8; test_dictation_e2e.sh 9 of 9; reload, 21 loaded. Version 1.3.0. Open: whether paragraphsFormat should be exported, or have a form that takes plain text.
2026-11-17: The user asked that the reformatting function be part of the Spoon. paragraphsFormat(segments, pause) is exported and documented under Methods; it returns the text, not the Spoon. Checked: reload, 21 loaded; hs.spoons['hs_whisper-gt'].paragraphsFormat(...) gives the expected text; make test-js 8 of 8.
close_reason: Implemented and committed in the configuration repository. Approved by the user.

title: Add optional timestamps and silence dropping to hs_whisper-gt's streaming recorder
description:
Implement the design decided in hammer2spoons-ei6.54 (see its notes).

1. The streaming server takes an optional per-recording setting, off by default. When it is on, a pause longer than the silence threshold is dropped, keeping a margin of speech before and after each stretch of speech (a setting, default 1 s), so that a long silence costs no transcription, disk or memory. Each stretch of speech becomes its own chunk, and chunk_ready carries its offset from the start of the recording, counted in samples.
2. All the data is kept: the full recording, written to disk as it is recorded rather than held in memory; a speech-only recording; and a JSON sidecar listing each stretch of speech with its start and end in both.
3. The Spoon asks the whisper server for verbose_json and puts [mm:ss] (or [h:mm:ss] past an hour) before each segment, at chunk offset plus segment start.
4. Only the streaming recorder. With a filter active, or a dictation to a processor, the Spoon reports an error and does not record.
5. A new function transcribes with timestamps.
6. The user's configuration keeps working: check use.status() before and after, and restart the streaming server, as CLAUDE.md requires.
acceptance_criteria: Timestamped dictation works with the streaming recorder and the whisper server; dictation without timestamps behaves as before; the configuration loads; the user has approved closing this bead.
notes:
2026-11-17: Implemented in ../Spoons/hs_whisper-gt (still in the parent repository), version 1.1.0, not committed.
- whisper_stream.py: drop_silence and speech_margin per recording; chunk_ready carries offset and duration; the full recording and the speech-only recording are written to disk as they arrive; a JSON sidecar is written at the end; complete_file names all three.
- init.js: config.streamingTimestamps (false) and streamingSpeechMargin (1.0); whisperserver.segments() uses verbose_json; transcribeTimestampedToggle(); refusals for another recorder or transcriber, a filter, or a processor; recordingsPrune() deletes the sidecar too.
- Parent init.js: command whisper-transcribe-timestamped-toggle.
- Readme documents it.
Checked: pytest 94 passed (7 new in test_drop_silence.py, 1 new in test_server_process.py); test_dictation_e2e.sh 7 of 7 with a new timestamped case; use.status() 21 loaded before and after; the two refusals leave the Spoon IDLE.
Known: a chunk's first timestamp can be up to speech_margin early, because Whisper starts the first segment at 0 and the chunk begins with the margin.
2026-11-17: Format changed at the user's request. Each chunk starts with a line '[C start end]', and each segment is '[start end] text'. Times are mm:ss, or h:mm:ss from an hour on. They come from the word times: a line runs from its first word to its last, and a chunk from its first word to its last. Words without a letter or digit are ignored, because Whisper places a final full stop at the end of the audio. Known: Whisper anchors a chunk's first word at the start of the audio, so a chunk's start can be up to speech_margin early; --dtw (see hammer2spoons-ei6.56 for the related server-start work) might fix that. Checked: test_dictation_e2e.sh 8 of 8; use.status() 21 loaded.
close_reason: Implemented and committed in the configuration repository (d0f4059). Approved by the user after trying it.

title: Investigate hs_whisper-gt's features and decide what to do next
description: Discuss with the user what hs_whisper-gt does today, which of its features are worth keeping, changing or dropping, and what to do next. The result is a decision, recorded in this bead's notes, that shapes hammer2spoons-ei6.24 (moving and reviewing the Spoon) and any new beads. No code changes are expected in this bead.
acceptance_criteria: The user has agreed on what to do next, the decisions are recorded in the notes, and the user has approved closing this bead.
notes:
2026-11-17: Timing information from the transcription. Nothing implemented; the user asked that nothing be implemented in this bead.

1. The Spoon asks the whisper.cpp server for response_format "text" (init.js:1326), so it receives only the text. The only timing it records is the warm-up time, in debug mode.
2. The server answers response_format "verbose_json" with the audio duration, segments with start and end, avg_logprob and no_speech_prob, words with start, end and probability, and the detected language with each language's probability. Checked by sending assets/silence.wav to 127.0.0.1:8080.
3. The server does not report how long it took to compute. That would be measured in the Spoon, around fetch().
4. The quarter second of silence was transcribed as " Thank you." with no_speech_prob near zero, the usual Whisper hallucination. The word probabilities might be used to catch it in real recordings.
5. The streaming server knows when each chunk starts and ends, but its chunk_ready event does not send those times.

Three kinds of timing were offered: transcription speed (audio seconds against compute seconds), timestamps in the text, and the delay from a pause to the paste with the streaming recorder. The user has not yet chosen.
2026-11-17: Decisions on timestamps and dropping silence. Nothing implemented.

The user wants segment timestamps on the transcription, and long silences that cost nothing.

How the streaming server handles silence now: every half-second block is kept, in the current chunk and in all_audio. A chunk is cut after streamingSilenceThreshold of silence, once it is at least streamingMinChunkDuration long, with the silence inside it. A long silence becomes a series of chunks of about 5 s without speech, written to disk but not transcribed (streamingSilentChunkSkip). all_audio holds float32 at 16 kHz in memory, 64 KB a second or about 230 MB an hour, until the recording ends.

Decided:
1. Optional. It is a parameter the Spoon sends to the server when a recording starts, like min_chunk_duration, and is off by default.
2. A margin of speech is kept before and after each stretch of speech, through a rolling buffer. It is a parameter, defaulting to 1 s.
3. Only a pause longer than the silence threshold is dropped. A shorter pause stays inside the chunk, so Whisper sees whole sentences.
4. Only the streaming recorder. sox gives no timestamps and drops nothing.
5. Each chunk carries its offset from the start of the recording, counted in samples, in chunk_ready. The Spoon asks the whisper server for verbose_json and puts [mm:ss] before each segment, at chunk offset plus segment start. No silence is removed inside a chunk, so that sum is the real time.
6. A sidecar file goes with the recording and lists where the speech is, so that the recording can be understood later.

Open:
- Point 4 of the user's answer was 'both', meaning the speech-only recording and the full recording. To be confirmed. If the full recording is kept, it should be written to disk as it is recorded, not held in all_audio, or the memory cost stays.
- What the sidecar holds and its format: for each stretch of speech, its start and end in the original recording and in the speech-only file, probably JSON.
- The timestamp format: time since the start, [mm:ss], or the clock time.
- Whether filters and processors receive the timestamps.
2026-11-17: The open points, decided. Nothing implemented.

1. All the data is kept: the full recording, the speech-only recording and the sidecar. It can be reduced later. The full recording is written to disk as it is recorded, not held in memory.
2. The sidecar is JSON. For each stretch of speech it gives its start and end in the full recording and in the speech-only file.
3. Timestamps are the offset from the start of the recording, as [mm:ss].
4. Timestamps do not work with filters for now. When timestamps are on and a filter is active, the Spoon reports an error and does not record.

Still open: whether the same applies to processors; and the format past an hour, presumably [h:mm:ss].
2026-11-17: Processors never receive timestamped text. To confirm: whether a dictation to a processor with timestamps on is refused with an error, as with filters, or goes ahead and the processor gets the text without timestamps.
2026-11-17: Decided: a dictation to a processor with timestamps on is refused, as with filters. The Spoon reports an error and does not record. Still open: the timestamp format past an hour, presumably [h:mm:ss].
close_reason: Discussion done; the decisions are in the notes, and the work they led to is hammer2spoons-ei6.55 and hammer2spoons-ei6.56. Approved by the user.

title: Add tests to hs_window-gt
description:
hs_window-gt has no tests. Every change to it is checked by hand, and the Spoon is used every day in the user's configuration, so a regression is found only when something goes wrong in use.

The tests live in Spoons/hs_window-gt.spoon2/tests/, which .gitattributes already marks export-ignore, so users do not download them. A makefile in the Spoon's directory, also export-ignored, runs them.

Most of the Spoon acts on real windows and screens through Hammerspoon 2, so most tests have to run inside the running Hammerspoon 2, sent through hs2. They must not disturb the user's configuration: they act only on windows the tests open themselves, and they restore any state the Spoon saves, such as the attached number keys.

The work is split into child beads: first the harness and the test window, then one bead per area of the Spoon.
acceptance_criteria: Every child bead is closed. make test in the Spoon's directory runs every test and reports each result. The use.status() check shows the same Spoons loaded before and after a test run, and the user's windows and attached keys are unchanged by it.

title: Bring forward only the chosen window when focusing a window of a multi-window application
description:
Reported by the user on 2026-11-15: Chrome has windows on two displays. Switching to one of them, sometimes but not always, also brings the other forward. Requirement, in the user's words: it should leave the other windows back; it should only bring forward the desired window.

Path: hs_selectWindow-gt -> hs_window-gt windowFocus() -> Hammerspoon 2 window.focus() (becomeMain, setFrontmost(allWindows: false), becomeMain again after 0.3 s, citing Chrome putting its previous main window back, upstream #356) + raise(), then hs_window-gt's own becomeMain() + raise() after config.focusReassertDelay. Likely cause: Chrome restores its previous main window, raising it on its display, and nothing lowers it again. hs_window-gt's comment that upstream reasserts only for Finder is out of date.

Plan: measure by hand which window is main and which is in front on each display before, right after, and 0.3 s after each switch; then fix, either by dropping the duplicate reassertion or by raising again the window that was in front on the other display.
notes:
Left for later by the user on 2026-11-15. Measurement prepared: a temporary wrapper around hs.spoons["hs_window-gt"].windowFocus, installed through hs2, which records before the switch and at 0.05, 0.35, 0.8 and 1.5 s after it the application's mainWindow and the front window on each screen (first per screen in hs.window.orderedWindows()). The user then switches to a Chrome window several times by hand. The before-snapshot costs about 0.1 s, which slightly changes the timing. Four screens on 2026-11-15: Built-in Retina Display, DELL U3225QE, EV2736W, Sidecar Display (AirPlay).
2026-11-23, found while testing hs_window-gt (hammer2spoons-cvl): hs.window.orderedWindows() in Hammerspoon 2 does not return windows in stacking order, although its documentation says 'in z-order'. orderedWindows() in Modules/hs.window/HSWindowModule.swift lists the frontmost application's windows first, then each other application's, from WindowEnumerator.windowServerWindowIDs(), which reads CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo in front-to-back order but stores the ids in a set per process, losing the order. hs_window-gt uses it in windowWithPreviousSwap, in windowPrevious's fallback and in windowToBackSend, which can therefore pick the wrong window when windows of different applications overlap. Seen on 2026-11-23: with Chrome focused, a Chrome window was taken as the front window of a screen where kitty covered it. This may explain part of this bead. Not filed upstream: the user decided to leave it as it is for now. The running build has no HSSpace.windowIDs() or currentSpace, so the true order is not available through the Spaces functions either.
2026-11-23, later: the running build (main with upstream through 3551af98) has HSSpace.windowIDs(), which lists a space's windows front to back; the test harness now takes each screen's front window from it (commit 16277b6). raise() brings one window in front of another application's window without activating its application (Music's window put back in front of Finder's). Hammerspoon 2's focus() now reasserts main status after 0.3 s for every application, citing Chrome (#356), so _windowFocus()'s own reassertion repeats it; its comment saying upstream does this only for Finder is out of date. Updated plan: record each display's front window with windowIDs() before the switch; after the reassertion, raise() again any display's previous front window that a window of the same application, not the chosen one, has covered. The three uses of orderedWindows() in hs_window-gt can also move to windowIDs().
2026-11-23: fixed in hs_window-gt 2.4.2. _windowFocus() records each screen's windows front to back before the switch; after 0.3 s it raises again any screen's previous front window that a window of the same application, not the chosen one, covered. Measured: Skim restored on the laptop 4 of 4, about 0.3 s after Chrome covered it. The second assertion skips a window closed in the meantime, which removed the Spoon's 'Failed to make window main' (AXError -25202); one remains from Hammerspoon 2's own focus() reassertion. windows, two-screens and connections tests: 48 of 48. Not done here: the reassertion that repeats upstream's, and the three uses of orderedWindows().

title: Leave the focused window out of hs_selectWindow-gt's choosers, as Hammerspoon 1 did
description:
The Hammerspoon 1 Spoon did not list the focused window in its chooser; the Hammerspoon 2 port never carried that over (checked in every version from de8ffc5 on 2026-09-11 to the move, f37f68e). Every chooser of hs_selectWindow-gt lists the focused window first and opens with it selected.

Fix: chooseFrom() and order() leave out the window at the front of focusOrder, which follows hs_windowfilter-gt's windowFocused events. The tracker's per-window state.focused flag must not be used for this: it can stay true on a window of another application after the focus has left it (seen on 2026-11-15: kitty in front, Chrome's EmacsWiki window still marked focused).

The same change set fixes a regression from bb11f7f (ei6.47.5): hs.chooser calls onHide before onSelect, so onSelect found its chooser no longer current and did not activate the chosen window.
notes: Commit 04e8a5c was amended to 296ae0d to correct the readme's windowPreviousSelect() passage.

title: Read the missing arguments of hs_window-gt's exported functions through hs_interactive-gt

title: Review the language and structure of the published Spoons' readmes
description:
Review the readme of every published Spoon, and the top-level readme, for language and structure.

Language: precise, technical terms throughout, never the casual everyday word (as found in hammer2spoons-ei6.41: requires rather than needs, options rather than buttons, selects rather than runs). No figurative language. Full sentences, one thing per sentence, the fact before its qualification, as CLAUDE.md's Writing section requires. Not condescending.

Structure: written from the user's point of view. Each readme opens with what the Spoon does for the user, then Installing, then the reference, with design notes and implementation after. The Spoons should follow the same order of sections, and use the same terms for the same things.

Also decide whether code identifiers and comments that use 'button' for a menu option (the buttons field, buttonImage()) should be renamed; that changes hs_menu-gt's interface and so needs the user's decision.

Published Spoons at the time of writing: hs_appleMusic-gt, hs_interactive-gt, hs_menu-gt, hs_selectWindow-gt, hs_window-gt, hs_windowfilter-gt. Each changed Spoon's version is raised.
notes:
Further requirements from the user (2026-11-15):
1. Immediately after the introduction, each readme has a list of the Spoon's most important features.
2. The text is impersonal. It does not address the reader: no 'you', and no 'You want...'.
3. Every section has at least one sentence introducing it, including reference sections such as Settings.
4. Every section is understandable on its own. For example, order() in hs_selectWindow-gt's readme is described too briefly to be understood: say what it returns, in what order, and what it is used for.
Also (user, 2026-11-15): a readme describes a function by how it is used and what for, before its mechanics. What it returns comes after, and only as far as it matters to that use (example: order() in hs_selectWindow-gt).
Also (user, 2026-11-15): no ambiguous pronouns. Where 'it', 'its', 'this' or 'they' could refer to more than one noun, repeat the noun.
Also (user, 2026-11-15): use the term of the domain rather than a vague word (an event is emitted and a handler invoked, never 'a report' or 'something happens'), and avoid choppy, staccato sentences. Done in hs_windowfilter-gt: the introduction and features are rewritten in terms of events, handlers, filters and observers, and the Events section lists each of the nineteen events on its own row. The other readmes still need the same pass, together with the check for ambiguous pronouns.

title: Document in hs_menu-gt how to add to a Spoon's menu
description:
Spoons such as hs_window-gt and hs_appleMusic-gt export their menu (menu) and open it with menuShow(). A configuration can add its own buttons to such a menu without changing the Spoon, as the user's menus.js does for the music menu:

    const musicMenu = () => [
        ...hs.spoons["hs_appleMusic-gt"].menu,
        ...[ { label: "Amps", key: "w", fn: ... } ]
    ]

Add a section to hs_menu-gt's readme, 'Adding to a Spoon's menu', that explains:
1. A Spoon's menu is an array of buttons (or an object whose buttons are under .buttons, as hs_window-gt's is), so a configuration copies it and adds, removes or reorders buttons.
2. Write the menu as a function, so it is built when it opens, when the Spoon is loaded after the file defining the menu.
3. Copy rather than change the Spoon's array; changing it also changes what the Spoon's menuShow() shows.
4. Letters must not collide with the Spoon's; the first button with a letter takes it.
Raise hs_menu-gt's version.

title: Analyze AeroSpace as an alternative for spaces
description:
AeroSpace (https://github.com/nikitabobko/AeroSpace) is another window manager for macOS. Analyze it as an alternative to yabai and to upstream hs.spaces (pull request #371), using the same questions this epic has asked of yabai. 1. What AeroSpace's workspaces are. Find out whether they are macOS Spaces or its own, and what that means for Mission Control and for other applications.
2. Whether it needs System Integrity Protection disabled, and which permissions it needs.
3. How a client talks to it. Find out whether it has a socket, what the protocol is, and whether a client can receive events without running a shell command for each one.
4. How it names workspaces, and whether names survive a restart. This matters because the Spoon identifies spaces by name.
5. Which of the functions in hs_yabai-gt/ai/hs1-spaces.org and the adopted features in yabai-extras.org it provides.
6. Its license, how it is maintained, and whether it works on macOS 27.
7. Whether it can be used without tiling, since tiling was left out of this epic.

Write the analysis in hs_yabai-gt/ai, and end it with a comparison of yabai, AeroSpace and hs.spaces from #371. Do not install AeroSpace without asking the user first.
acceptance_criteria: The analysis answers all seven questions with sources, and ends with the comparison. The user has approved closing this bead.
notes: Analysis in hs_yabai-gt/ai/aerospace.org, from the clone at ~/git.w/AeroSpace (commit 6ed6af62). AeroSpace emulates workspaces by moving hidden windows off-screen instead of using macOS Spaces; needs no SIP; its socket keeps connections open, has a documented protocol and a subscribe command that streams events as JSON; workspace names persist in its config. title: Record findings on yabai's socket, its license, and upstream hs.spaces
description:
While discussing the evaluation in eqg.3, several findings came up that change the direction of the epic. Record them in hs_yabai-gt/ai:

1. yabai's socket answers one request per connection and never writes to a client, so events reach a client only through a shell command run by a signal. A measurement showed that a request over the socket costs far less than running yabai -m as a process.
2. yabai and Hammerspoon 2 are both under the MIT license.
3. Hammerspoon 2 already has hs.socket, which supports Unix domain sockets, and hs.window already uses a private SkyLight function.
4. Upstream Hammerspoon 2 has an open pull request, #371, that ports hs.spaces from Hammerspoon 1 without needing SIP disabled, and an issue, #86, about switching spaces with synthesized swipes. The pull request lacks moving a window to a space and instant switching, both of which yabai has.
acceptance_criteria: The findings are written up in hs_yabai-gt/ai with their sources. The user has approved closing this bead.
notes: Written: the socket's one-request behaviour, the cost measurement and the events section in hs_yabai-gt/ai/yabai.org; the licenses, hs.socket, PR #371 and issue #86 in hs_yabai-gt/ai/upstream-hs-spaces.org. Question 1 of eqg.3 is answered there: hs.socket supports Unix domain sockets.

2026-11-26: confirmed with a real application. The user ran TextEdit with five document windows and hid it: all five report subrole AXDialog and isStandard false, and a filter with allowRoles: 'AXStandardWindow' lists none of them. 2026-11-26: TextEdit confirmed for minimizing too: visible AXStandardWindow, minimized AXDialog, restored AXStandardWindow. Second finding, in Hammerspoon 2: after TextEdit was unhidden, its five windows reported AXStandardWindow, but a filter with allowRoles: "AXStandardWindow" still excluded the four that had not been minimized, 5 s later (isWindowAllowed false too). WindowTracker.applicationHiddenChanged() (WindowTracker.swift:426) only sets isAppHidden on each window's state and does not read the window again, so the subrole read while the application was hidden (AXDialog) is kept until another notification (move, resize, title, minimize) makes the tracker read the window. title: Why some windows cannot be found or acted on: window objects come only from the Accessibility API
description:
Findings of 2026-11-25, recorded so that a window that is missing from hs.window can be explained later.

1. A window object is an Accessibility element. In Hammerspoon 2, HSWindow wraps the window's AXUIElement: HSWindow(element: element, app: app). Its title, frame, isStandard, focus(), moving and resizing all go through that element.

2. The window server knows every window, whatever the application allows: its id, its owner's pid, its frame, its layer, and (with Screen Recording) its title and picture. Hammerspoon 2 reads it for HSSpace.windowIDs(), the Space type (currentSpace.type), snapshotForID(), and the first step of hs.window.forID(). But it has no window object built from the window server alone.

3. hs.window.forID(id) (Modules/hs.window/HSWindowModule.swift, lines 310-327) asks the window server which process owns the window, then asks that application through the Accessibility API for its windows and picks the one with that id. If the application does not answer, the list is empty and forID() returns null.

4. Measured with the kiosk Firefox (pid 61637, -P kioskmini --kiosk, fullscreen on the iPad), which turns its Accessibility API off (kAXErrorAPIDisabled, -25211):
   1. hs.window.focusedWindow(): null.
   2. hs.window.frontmostWindow() (new in #469): Finder's desktop, id 0, not standard. Wrong: the desktop did not have the focus.
   3. hs.application.frontmost(): Firefox pid 61637, found from macOS's list of running applications, not the Accessibility API; its focusedWindow and mainWindow are null.
   4. The system-wide Accessibility element: null for the focused application.
   5. The window server: focused Space 1408 on the Sidecar screen, holding windows 16129 and 3232; forID() gives null for both.

5. isStandard reads the window's subrole through the Accessibility API, and returns false when it cannot be read. So true always means the application answered and called the window standard; false means either not standard or not answered.

6. Hammerspoon 1 had the same restriction. Its HSapplication allWindows (Hammerspoon/HSuicore.m, line 192) reads kAXWindowsAttribute, and HSwindow is built with initWithAXUIElementRef. hs.window.orderedWindows() takes only the order from the window server (CGWindowList ids) and the windows themselves from the Accessibility API. A slow or hung application delayed every window listing in both, because each application is asked in turn; Hammerspoon 1 had hs.window.timeout() for that, and Hammerspoon 2 sets a 0.25 s timeout while listing.

7. macOS allows moving, resizing and focusing another application's window only through the Accessibility API, so an application that turns it off cannot have its windows controlled by any tool. A read-only window object built from the window server (id, owner, frame, title) would be possible, and would be a feature request upstream, not a defect.

Workarounds in use: the Space type for fullscreen detection (hammer2spoons-xov); listing such an application as '(windows are not accessible)' in hs_selectWindow-gt (hammer2spoons-ei6.65); the test harness going back to the Space, since the window cannot be raised (hammer2spoons-8xv). See also the memory kiosk-firefox-ax-off.
notes: 2026-11-25, the general case: without the Accessibility API, another application's window can still be read from the window server, and possibly moved by (1) Apple Events, through the application's own scripting (set bounds of front window), which is a separate channel, if the application is scriptable; (2) synthetic mouse drags on its title bar, not for fullscreen or borderless windows; (3) the window server's private functions run inside the Dock, as yabai's scripting addition does, which needs SIP partly off. Options 1 and 2 are described from how macOS works and were not tried.

title: Remove Spoons/lib/shell.js; call hs.task.runAsync() directly
description:
Decided by the user on 2026-11-25, while working on hammer2spoons-cdd.16.

Context: shell.js wrapped hs.task.create() so that every command resolved to {out, err, code} and never rejected. It was written for two Hammerspoon 2 limitations: hs.task.runAsync() rejected with a plain object, not an Error (upstream #446), and it could not write to standard input (#447). Both were fixed upstream (#458, #461).

What was tried first: a test of what the 18 callers relied on (12 cases), then a rewrite of shell.js on runAsync(). Today's shell.js failed 3 cases (a missing command never settled; cat with no input never settled; commandStart() of a missing command returned a task, not null); the rewrite passed all 12. I recommended keeping the rewritten module, because 18 calls in six files would otherwise each need their own try/catch and existence check.

Decision: the user chose to remove shell.js. Each caller now calls hs.task.runAsync() directly (hs_emacs-gt, hs_hass-gt, hs_jp-gt, hs_url-gt, lib/authinfo.js); init.js keeps a three-line shellRunLogging() for its three calls; hs_whisper-gt, with ten calls and two long-running tasks, has local commandResult() and taskStart(). Configuration commit 3d7c48e.

Consequences to remember:
1. A command named in the settings is checked with hs.fs.exists() before it runs, in each caller. hs.task never settles the promise of a command it cannot start (upstream fault, hammer2spoons-aaj). When upstream fixes it, these checks can go.
2. Use hs.fs.exists(), not hs.fs.isFile(): isFile() is false for a symbolic link, and Homebrew installs commands as links. The first rewrite used isFile() and broke emacsclient for a few minutes.
3. runAsync() resolves only on exit status 0; anything else rejects with an Error holding exitCode, stdout and stderr. A caller that wants the output of a failing command reads it from the error.
4. A long-running command (a server, a recorder) still needs hs.task.create(): runAsync() is for commands that finish.

Revisit if: many new callers appear that repeat the same try/catch, or upstream adds a way to run a command that never rejects.

title: Use hs_windowfilter-gt's windows instead of hs.window.allWindows() where it makes sense
description:
Found on 2026-11-24 while checking ei6.63. hs.window.allWindows() asks every application for its windows, which takes about 0.1 s, and much longer while an application does not answer (Music took 5 to 8 s per request during a library sync, 2026-11-23). hs_windowfilter-gt already holds the windows, and reading them costs about 1 ms. Candidates:
1. hs_window-gt, allApplicationWindows() (init.js around line 156), used by the number keys attached to windows (lines around 1432, 1490, 1533) to find an attached window again.
2. hs_window-gt, coveredFrontWindowsRaise() (around line 301, from ei6.50), which looks up the windows by id after a display's front window changed.
3. hs_interactive-gt, readers.window.prompted and the fullscreen screens (around lines 366 and 436): they already use hs_windowfilter-gt when it is loaded, and fall back to orderedWindows()/allWindows() without it. hs_interactive-gt does not require hs_windowfilter-gt, so the fallback stays.
For each, check what the filter's list leaves out that the call needs: hs_windowfilter-gt tracks only standard applications and leaves out windows without a title that are not standard, and an attached window or a covered front window may be one of those. Keep hs_windowfilter-gt's own scan, which is the source of its list. Not in scope: the three uses of orderedWindows() in hs_window-gt, which need the stacking order (ei6.63). Each change in its own commit, so that a bug can be traced to it.

title: hs_selectWindow-gt: functions for other scripts to find and focus windows by title or application
description: Parity with the Hammerspoon 1 Spoon (~/.hammerspoon/Spoons/hs_select_window.spoon/init.lua, around lines 175-222 and 618), which exported helpers for scripts: findByTitle(t) returns the first window whose title matches t; focusByTitle(t) focuses it and alerts when t is missing; focusByApp(appName) focuses the first window of an application whose name matches; focusByAppAndTitle(appName, title) focuses the first window of the application of exactly that name whose title matches; nextFullScreen() focuses the next fullscreen window other than the focused one, and alerts when there is none. Lua's string.find takes a pattern; decide between a string, a RegExp or both, as applicationByBundleSelect() does. Rename them by the repository's conventions (subject first, action last; Select for those that focus a window), for example windowByTitleFind, windowByTitleSelect, applicationByNameSelect, applicationWindowByTitleSelect and fullscreenWindowNextSelect, and agree the names with the user before writing them. Look in the windows the tracker holds, most recently used first, focus through hs_window-gt's windowFocus(), and return the window or null. Document them in the readme as functions for other scripts, with examples, add them to the 'Coming from Hammerspoon 1' table, and test them.

title: hs_selectWindow-gt: the chooser's key moves the selection when pressed again, and a single row is switched to without a chooser
description: Parity with the Hammerspoon 1 Spoon (~/.hammerspoon/Spoons/hs_select_window.spoon/init.lua). (1) While its chooser was open, pressing the key that opened it again moved the selection down one row, and the same key with Shift moved it up (bindHotkeys(), around line 724: the modal keys sent Ctrl-N and Ctrl-P, which the chooser takes as down and up). hs_selectWindow-gt binds only Tab and Shift+Tab while a chooser is open (takeSessionKeys()). Bind each key given to bindHotkeys() as a session key that moves the selection, release them with the chooser, and check that this does not fight the hotkey itself, which is bound globally. (2) When the list had a single row, Hammerspoon 1 switched to it at once without showing a chooser (around line 418). Decide whether hs_selectWindow-gt should do the same, perhaps as a setting, since a chooser with one row still lets the user cancel. Document and test both.

title: hs_selectWindow-gt: settings for the chooser's text size

Add camelCase settings for them (null keeping the chooser's default), apply them in chooseFrom(), document them in the settings table, correct the 'Coming from Hammerspoon 1' section, and test that the chooser receives them.

title: Move the Spoons' hand-written bindHotkeys() to Hammerspoon 2's generic one (upstream #441)
description: Upstream pull request #441 (6e8c19e5, in the running build since 2026-11-24) lets a Spoon export 'bindings', its hotkey actions keyed by name (a function, or { pressed, released, repeat, message }). hs.spoons.load() then gives it a generic bindHotkeys(mapping), which takes [mods, key, message] or { mods, key, message }, replaces an action's hotkey when it is bound again, unbinds with null or false, throws EINVALIDARG before binding anything when the mapping is wrong, and is used by use()'s hotkeys option, including 'default' with defaultHotkeys. When a Spoon exports both, 'bindings' wins and the console gets a warning. On 2026-11-24, 5 Spoons in this repository write their own bindHotkeys(). For each: check whether 'bindings' expresses what it does (modal hotkeys cannot be), move it, keep its tests passing (several test that a second call releases the first call's keys and that an unknown name throws), update its readme, and raise its version. Check how the user's configuration binds keys through use() before changing anything. Consider whether the Spoons should keep working on builds without #441.
notes: 2026-11-24, decided by the user: keep each Spoon's own bindHotkeys(). Upstream's generic one (hs.spoons.js makeBindHotkeys(), from #441) differs: (1) a second call replaces only the actions it names, while ours release every key of the first call, as the readmes and tests say; (2) its hotkeys are private to it, so a Spoon's stop() cannot release them except by calling bindHotkeys() again with null for each action; (3) a key that cannot be bound throws part-way, where ours log and continue; (4) it exists only on a Spoon loaded by hs.spoons.load(), so the test harness, which loads a fresh copy itself, would have to imitate that; (5) builds without #441 would have no bindHotkeys() at all; (6) hs_selectWindow-gt's bindHotkeys() records the key running (keyNow) and the keys bound (bindingsShow), which bindings cannot express. It would add messages, released and repeat callbacks and defaultHotkeys, which no Spoon here uses. Revisit if a Spoon needs one of those.

title: Stop retrying, and warn once, for an application that has turned the Accessibility API off
description: hs_windowfilter-gt retries hs.ax.on() five times for an application it cannot watch, then logs an error, after every configuration load. On 2026-11-23 this came from a Firefox started in kiosk mode (-P kioskmini --kiosk), which has turned the Accessibility API off: its AXRole reads null and its windows cannot be listed. The normal Firefox is watched. Plan: when hs.ax.on() fails with kAXErrorAPIDisabled, stop retrying and log one warning that the application has disabled accessibility. hs.ax.on()'s Error carries no code today; the only way found to get it is to set an attribute no application has (setAttributeValue('NoSuchAttribute', false) gives kAXErrorAPIDisabled for the kiosk, kAXErrorAttributeUnsupported for the normal one). The user decided on 2026-11-23 not to use that workaround, and to wait for the upstream issue drafted in the configuration's ai/issue_unfiled_ax-on-error-code.md, which asks hs.ax.on() to put the code in err.code.
notes: 2026-11-23: filed upstream as https://github.com/Hammerspoon/Hammerspoon2/issues/437 (draft in the configuration's ai/issue_437_ax-on-error-code.md). Resume when hs.ax.on() puts the Accessibility error in err.code.

title: hs_window-gt: use the windows' real stacking order in windowWithPreviousSwap, windowPrevious and windowToBackSend
description:
Left from hammer2spoons-ei6.50. hs_window-gt uses hs.window.orderedWindows() in windowWithPreviousSwap, in windowPrevious's fallback and in windowToBackSend. orderedWindows() lists the frontmost application's windows first, not the stacking order, so these can pick the wrong window when windows of different applications overlap. HSSpace.windowIDs() gives the order front to back, as screenWindowIdsRecord() in the Spoon and frontWindowsRecord() in the test harness now use. Its second part, reviewing windowFocus()'s second assertion, moved to hammer2spoons-ei6.72.

Pre-approved by the user on 2026-11-24: when new tests that use windows of two applications overlapping fail with the current code and pass after the change, and the existing tests still pass, the bead is committed and closed without asking. Anything that needs the user's help or decision still comes back for approval.

title: Keep a window that comes forward after the restore from covering the user's front window
description: On 2026-11-23, after a run of four hs_window-gt test files (connections, placements, windows, two-screens), the laptop's front window was Finder #59055 instead of Music #59121, which had been in front before the run. raise() on the Music window afterwards put it back in front of Finder, so raise() itself works. Not verified: a guess is that macOS activates Finder a moment after the fixture ends the last test windows' processes, after the harness has already raised the recorded windows. The one-test file tests/selftest/focus.test.js did not show it. Check the guess, for example by recording the front windows just after the restore and again 1 s later, and if it holds, wait for the test windows' processes to end before restoring.
close_reason: Seen once and not reproduced; the user does not think the defect exists. Closed at the user's decision, 2026-11-23.

title: Keep an application that does not answer from holding the start chooser
description: On 2026-11-23 the start chooser of tests/run stayed on screen for about 7 s after the user's choice. The harness records the front windows synchronously right after it, with hs.window.orderedWindows(), which waits out the full Accessibility timeout for an application that does not answer: Music, during a library sync, took 4.5 to 8 s; without it the call took 0.1 s. hs.window.allWindows() limits each request to 0.25 s. Proposed: (1) wait 0.3 s after the choice so the chooser closes first; (2) use allWindows() instead of orderedWindows() in frontWindowsRecord(), with HSSpace.windowIDs() for the order; (3) read the window list once per restore, not once per window in windowExists(). Then sync every Spoon's copy. Possibly also an upstream issue: orderedWindows() and HSApplication.allWindows do not use the 0.25 s timeout.
close_reason: Not a defect of the harness: the delay came from Music not answering the Accessibility API during a library sync. With the sync off, orderedWindows() takes about 0.1 s. Closed at the user's decision, 2026-11-23.

title: Make the fixture's promptCancel() cancel a modal prompt
description: tests-common's fixture.js promptCancel() waits for the prompt with promises, which do not resolve while a modal prompt of hs_interactive-gt is open, and it sends one Escape, while the user's configuration needs two to close a dialog. In hs_countdown-gt's readme-review test it left the prompt open and the run waiting (2026-11-23). Rewrite it to use hs.timer callbacks set before the prompt opens, sending a second Escape when the prompt is still open, then sync every Spoon's copy with tests-common/sync and rerun the tests that call it.

title: Follow up upstream issue #391: Escape does not close hs.ui.textPrompt
description:
Upstream issue https://github.com/cmsj/Hammerspoon2/issues/391 (filed from hammer2spoons-ei6.52) was closed on 2026-11-19 without a fix. The maintainer wrote that Escape dismissed the dialog when he tested it, that Tab not moving the focus is probably normal AppKit behaviour, and asked to reopen it if he had missed something.

No commit has touched Modules/hs.ui upstream since 7efbe802, the commit the issue was reported against, so the difference lies in how the prompt was tested, not in the code. hs_interactive-gt has no workaround for it.

What to do:
1. Retest by hand on the current build (af2b6a59 or later) with the snippet in ~/.config/Hammerspoon2/ai/issue_391_textprompt-escape.md: once with Hammerspoon 2 frontmost, and once opened from a hotkey while another application is frontmost, as readers.number.prompted and readers.string.prompted are used.
2. If Escape now works in both, record that here and close this bead.
3. If it fails in one of them, find what differs from the maintainer's test (frontmost application, how the prompt is opened, macOS 27). Draft a short comment for #391 that gives the exact steps, for the user to review and post, and ask the maintainer to reopen it. Follow the AI disclosure rule in CLAUDE.md.
4. Drop the Tab part unless the user wants to pursue it.
notes:
2026-11-20: Retested by hand on af2b6a59. Test 1 (Hammerspoon 2 frontmost): Escape did not close the prompt. It put an 'I' into the text field, and only clicking Cancel closed it (button 1). The cause is on this machine, not in Hammerspoon 2. ~/Library/KeyBindings/DefaultKeyBinding.dict binds "\033" (Escape) as an Emacs-style prefix key (ESC-f, ESC-b, ESC-ESC = complete:, ...). Every Cocoa text field reads that file, so the prompt's field editor takes Escape as the start of a key sequence, and cancelOperation: never reaches the alert's Cancel button. The maintainer does not have this binding, which is why Escape worked for him. Closing #391 was correct. Test 2 (opened while kitty was frontmost) was not completed: the hs2 call blocked while the prompt was open.
Test 2 (opened while kitty was frontmost) gave the same result as test 1: Cancel (button 1), with 'I' in the field. Its hs2 call returned only after the prompt was closed.
User's screenshot (hs_countdown-gt's minutes prompt): one Escape does nothing visible. title: Give hs_whisper-gt's whisper server a VAD model
description:
whisper.cpp's server has its own voice-activity detection: the per-request field vad=true, with vad_threshold, vad_min_speech_duration_ms, vad_min_silence_duration_ms, vad_max_speech_duration_s and the speech padding. It works only when the server was started with --vad-model <file> (server.cpp:936). The user's server runs without one: ~/.emacs.d/modules/whisper-cli/build/bin/whisper-server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 --model /usr/local/whisper/ggml-model.bin.

The whisper.cpp checkout has models/download-vad-model.sh, which downloads a ggml Silero model. Only a test model, for-tests-silero-v6.2.0-ggml.bin, is there now.

1. Download a Silero VAD model in ggml format and decide where it is kept, for example beside the Whisper models in /usr/local/whisper.
2. Find out who starts the running server. The Spoon starts one only when nothing answers and whisperserverCmd is set (init.js, around line 1275); it passes no VAD option. Add a setting, such as whisperserverVadModelPath, that adds --vad-model when it is set, and document it.
3. Measure, with the test fixtures and with a real dictation, what vad=true changes: the text (for example the 'Thank you.' invented for silence), the segment and word times, and the transcription time. Decide whether the Spoon should send vad=true, and when.
4. Keep the configuration working: check use.status() before and after, and restart the whisper server, as CLAUDE.md requires.

Context: hammer2spoons-ei6.54 (feature discussion) and hammer2spoons-ei6.55 (timestamps). The streaming server already drops silence with its own Silero VAD, so this VAD matters mostly for the sox recorder, for transcribeAgain on a full recording, and for silence left inside a chunk.
acceptance_criteria: The model is installed; the Spoon can start the server with it; the measurements are recorded in the notes, with a decision on sending vad=true; the configuration loads; the user has approved closing this bead.
notes:
2026-11-17: Moved from hammer2spoons-ei6.55. Whisper places a chunk's first word at the start of the audio, which is the speech margin, so a timestamped chunk's start can be up to speech_margin early. Measure whether vad=true, or starting the server with --dtw, gives the first word its real start time. The user decided on 2026-11-17 that the VAD model should be added.
2026-11-17: Measured. Nothing implemented yet.

Model: models/ggml-silero-v6.2.0.bin in ~/.emacs.d/modules/whisper-cli, downloaded with models/download-vad-model.sh (865 KB). /usr/local/whisper belongs to root. The running whisper server is started by the Spoon, as a child of Hammerspoon 2, and restarted on every reload.

Test server on port 8081, three test chunks of the long fixture. The reference is where the sound is in each chunk: 0.75-3.80 s, 1.20-10.15 s and 1.30-6.05 s.

1. As now: segments and words start at 0; the first word is anchored at the start of the audio. About 1.1-1.3 s a chunk.
2. --dtw large.v3.turbo: needs flash attention off (-nfa), or the server turns DTW off. The word start and end fields do not change. The accurate times are in t_dtw, in hundredths of a second: 0.98-3.92, 1.36-9.96, 1.40-5.88. Segment times become wrong, for example 1.28-10.30 s in a 7.5 s file. About 20% slower. One chunk came back as '1 2 3 4 5 6'.
3. vad=true with --vad-model, flash attention on: segment times are mapped back to the chunk and are accurate: 0.74-4.09, 1.28-3.22 and 3.22-10.05, 1.31-6.21. Word times and t_dtw are not mapped back; they are in the shortened audio, so they cannot be used. Segments break at pauses: 'And then I want to have a second chunk.' | 'But it would be nice...'. The same speed or faster. The quarter second of silence gives no text instead of 'Thank you.'.
4. vad=true on the whole 43.5 s fixture: the text is better ('see what', not 'see you what'), but the segment times are wrong across the long gaps: the last segment is given 21.30 s, where the speech is at about 30 s. So VAD times are reliable within a chunk, not across a long recording with long pauses.

Recommendation to the user: start the server with --vad-model (new setting), keep flash attention, no --dtw. Send vad=true for timestamped chunks, and take the line and heading times from the segments rather than the words when it is on. Whether to send vad=true for ordinary dictation too, for the 'Thank you.' and the better text, is the user's decision.
2026-11-17: Implemented, not committed. The user does not need word times, only line and chunk times.
- New setting whisperserverVadModelPath. A server the Spoon starts gets --vad-model; transcribers.whisperserver.vad records that, and only then are timestamped requests sent vad=true (a server without the model answers HTTP 500). Flash attention stays on; no --dtw.
- Line and C times now come from the segments, not the words. Word parsing removed.
- diagnose() says whether the server has a VAD model. Readme documents it. Version 1.2.0.
- Configuration: whisperserverVadModelPath set to ~/.emacs.d/modules/whisper-cli/models/ggml-silero-v6.2.0.bin.
Checked: reload, 21 loaded; the server runs with --vad-model; test_dictation_e2e.sh 8 of 8, with times [C 00:00 00:04], [C 00:12 00:21], [C 00:30 00:35], against sound at 0.75-3.80, 12.20-21.15 and 30.30-35.05 s.
Open: whether ordinary dictation should also send vad=true (the user's decision).
2026-11-17: The user decided that ordinary dictation uses the VAD too. New setting whisperserverVad (default true); every request asks for vad=true when the server has the model, except warm(), which must reach the model. An empty answer with the VAD is the text, not an error; segments() returns [] for it.

Found: whisper-server (build 679bdb53, 2026-01-05) crashes when its first request is verbose_json with vad=true on audio without speech. text and json do not crash, and the same verbose_json request after any other request returns empty segments. My curl test crashed the user's server this way; a reload restarted it. The Spoon now awaits warm() as soon as it has started a server, so warm() is always first. Candidate for a whisper.cpp issue, after checking a current build; not a Hammerspoon 2 issue.

Checked: reload, 21 loaded; server with --vad-model survives the crashing request; silence gives '' and []; test_dictation_e2e.sh 8 of 8.
close_reason: VAD model added and used by default; committed in the configuration repository (b5bffb3). Approved by the user.

title: Draft an upstream issue: Escape does not close hs.ui.textPrompt
description:
Found on 2026-11-15 while testing hs_countdown-gt's startAsk(): pressing Escape in an hs.ui.textPrompt dialog does not close it; only clicking Cancel does. The user confirmed this by hand. It affects every dialog hs_interactive-gt shows (readers.number.prompted, readers.string.prompted).

What the source shows (Hammerspoon 2 at 7efbe802, Modules/hs.ui/Dialogs/HSUITextPrompt.swift, show(), lines 133-152): the prompt is an NSAlert with an NSTextField as its accessoryView, and buttons added in order with addButton(withTitle:). NSAlert gives a button titled Cancel the Escape key equivalent. The likely cause, not yet confirmed, is that the text field has the keyboard focus and its field editor handles Escape (cancelOperation:) without passing it to the alert's Cancel button. Verify this before filing, for example with a minimal hs.ui.textPrompt and a hand-pressed Escape, and check whether an issue already exists.

Follow 'Workarounds, and when to ask upstream' in CLAUDE.md and the repository's AI_POLICY.md: the draft is reviewed and edited by the user, and ends with an AI disclosure. Add it to hammer2spoons-ei6.28 if that bead collects the upstream drafts.

title: Draft upstream issues for the Hammerspoon 2 limitations found
description:
Collect the limitations in Hammerspoon 2 found during this epic and draft issues for those worth raising, following the rules in CLAUDE.md and AI_POLICY.md (check for existing issues, state only what was verified, end with an AI disclosure). Found so far:

1. hs.spoons has no way to declare dependencies between Spoons.
2. hs.task.runAsync() rejects with a plain object rather than an Error, so err.message is undefined in a conventional catch.
3. hs.task.runAsync() has no option for writing to a command's standard input.

The user files them, after reviewing and editing them.
acceptance_criteria: The user has reviewed the result and approved closing this bead.
notes:
The parent's features-missing.org lists Hammerspoon 2 features found missing while porting: no window lookup by identifier (still true on 2026-11-14: hs.window has snapshotForID but no lookup), one Spoon directory and no search path (why hs_interactive-gt has spoonsLoadPath), and no -c option in the hs2 command-line tool (still absent from hs2 -h). Check each against current Hammerspoon 2 and existing issues.
Candidate found in ei6.8: Hammerspoon 2 has no equivalent of Hammerspoon 1's hs.window.filter, and no issue or pull request asks for one (checked 2026-11-14). hs_windowfilter-gt provides it as a Spoon.
From the hs_window-gt review: HSCanvasModule.swift says a canvas is placed in AppKit coordinates (y = 0 at the bottom) and that hs.screen uses the same, but hs.screen frames are used together with window frames, which have y = 0 at the top. Check and raise if the documentation or the API is inconsistent.
From the hs_interactive-gt review (ai/review-hs_interactive-gt.org, items 4-6), workarounds that remain because Hammerspoon 2 lacks something: (1) hs.ui.textPrompt is a plain window, not a non-activating panel as hs.chooser is, so it cannot take the keyboard while Hammerspoon is in the background, and the Spoon brings Hammerspoon forward first; (2) hs.chooser exposes neither its frame nor its window, so the Spoon copies the arithmetic that places it; (3) a chooser created while another is closing does not take the keyboard, so commands that open one wait (runDelay).
